Take the lead in shaping the future of rural health at Southern.

What you'll be doing

The After Hours Nurse Manager coordinates after-hours patient care services including movements into, through and out of inpatient units across the Facilities. This position leads and supports after hours clinical staff by redeploying and coordinating replacement staff to achieve a seamless patient, client or consumer journey.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Selection Criteria

Current Registration with the Australian Health Practitioners Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse.

Relevant management qualification and-or equivalent experience.

Well-developed interpersonal, verbal and written communication, consultation and negotiation skills necessary to build and maintain collaborative relationships with individuals and other health professionals.

Proven ability to provide leadership and direction to staff with demonstrated capacity to manage clinical services, apply problem solving strategies and support continuous quality improvement.

Demonstrated experience and ability to contribute to service development, planning and change management.

Demonstrated ability to implement and monitor nursing resource allocations, FTE and workload to meet facility performance requirements.

Proven ability to function effectively as part of team and to work successfully with other professionals and disciplines.

Junior Draftsperson available in all states NSW, Qld, Vic, & WA

At NEPEAN™ we are proud to be Australia’s leading privately owned engineering, mining services and industrial manufacturing organisation. We have unique capabilities to deliver high value, innovative and sustainable solutions for the world’s leading mining, construction, and transport companies. Over the last 40 years, hard work, technical credibility, and a willingness to tackle very difficult projects have earned NEPEAN an enviable reputation. Today our organisation employs over 1400 people across six continents and distributes products to more than 65 countries.

We service our customers through multiple businesses in our portfolio: NEPEAN Building and Infrastructure (Galserv, Galintel, Weldlok), NEPEAN Engineering and Innovation, NEPEAN Power, Mining (NEPEAN Longwall), PROK, NEPEAN Conveyors, NEPEAN Transport, Gurtec, Roxon, and NEPEAN Belting Mackay.

Our Opportunity
Due to exponential growth, Nepean is seeking Junior Draftsperson to join their respective teams located in NSW, Qld, Vic, & WA.
This position will support the development and execution of project plans which could include conceptual design, prototyping, design for reliability and manufacturability, interfacing with vendors, qualification testing and documentation.

Your daily duties will include however are not limited to;
3D modelling and sketching up designs using input from engineers and senior designers on the team.
Calculate factors like tolerances, dimensioning, weldability and ease of assembly.
Create designs in line with company procedures, regulations and client standards.
Creating component and assembly models based on technical specifications (Autodesk Inventor).
Provide practical and engineered design solutions in consultations with lead engineers.
Deliver designs according to required timeframes and in line with company procedures, regulations, and client standards
Involvement from concept to install, including exposure to in-house fabrication workshop.
Demonstrate high standard of personal safety and safe design practices.
Assist mechanical engineers in the modelling and detailing of mechanical equipment.
Ensures that designs and finished work are within scope of work and allocated time frame.
Prepares general assembly drawings and designs for mechanical engineering work under the direction of senior engineers.
Use customer feedback and data to upgrade, improve or repair the company's existing machines.
Liaison with stakeholders
Provide support during the building and installation process, ensuring that the machine is built according to design specifications
To work in a safe manner using appropriate Safe Work Instructions or Safety Operating Procedures
Work in a collaborative and team manner.
Understand NEPEAN’s goals and core values.
Proactive and willing to take on new challenges.
Work effectively under pressure.

To be considered for this opportunity, the right person will have:
Experience within a similar role
Appropriate qualification/training.
Obtained drawing and design experience.
Technical competence
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated good oral and written communication.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Rights to work in Australia

If you're ready for your next challenge, please "Apply Now" and forward through your interest today!

Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

NEPEAN believes in diversity and is committed to providing Equal Employment opportunities for all applicants. We welcome applicants from all walks of life, including various socio-economic, cultural, LGBTIQ, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.

Job description:

 
Department of Health seeks an IT Officer - Network Communications to support network, Wi-Fi, communications and connectivity services.

 

 






 

The Team

Digital Infrastructure Services provides the foundational technology platforms that keep Tasmania's public health system connected, secure and operational. The team delivers and supports enterprise data centres, compute and storage platforms, virtualisation, data protection, network connectivity, Wi-Fi and core infrastructure services that underpin clinical, corporate and business systems across the state.

Working in a complex 24 7 always-on health environment, the team plays a critical role in service reliability, cyber resilience, asset lifecycle management, infrastructure modernisation, and the delivery of technology that directly supports frontline care. This is your opportunity to join a high-performing team delivering Digital Infrastructure services to hospitals, health facilities, clinicians, staff and the Tasmanian community.

The Role

Join Digital Infrastructure Services and help support the network and communications services that keep Tasmania's public health system connected, secure and operational.

In this entry-level role, you will assist with the day-to-day support of enterprise network, communications, Wi-Fi and connectivity services across a large 24 7 health environment. Working with an experienced team, you will support incidents and service requests, assist with troubleshooting, maintain documentation, liaise with stakeholders, and coordinate with vendors and service providers.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their ICT career to build practical experience in enterprise networking and communications while contributing to services that directly support hospitals, clinicians, staff and the Tasmanian community.

You will need

A sound foundation in IT and networking concepts, with an interest in communications, connectivity and infrastructure support.

The ability to support service delivery, including troubleshooting issues, assisting with incidents and service requests, and working effectively with team members, vendors and service providers.

Strong communication, teamwork and organisational skills, with the ability to follow documented processes and work effectively in a busy environment with competing priorities.

Permanent full time, day worker (with on call) position, working 76 hours per fortnight, commencing as soon as possible.

Experienced Leading Hand for road and asphalt projects. Lead crews, subcontractors and traffic control Teams!   Your new company  
 Our client is a leading civil infrastructure contractor delivering road construction, maintenance, and asphalt projects throughout Queensland. With a strong pipeline of ongoing work and a commitment to safety and quality, they are seeking an experienced Leading Hand to join their team and oversee multiple crews across active project sites. 
  Your new role  
 As a Leading Hand, you will be responsible for supervising a crew of approximately 12-13 personnel while coordinating daily activities across road construction and asphalt projects. You will provide leadership on-site, ensure work is completed safely and efficiently, liaise with subcontractors, manage traffic control operations, and support project supervisors with the successful delivery of works. This role will involve both local and away work, with projects requiring employees to work away for up to two weeks at a time. 
 Travel time is paid from the moment you leave Mackay, with transport provided in a company vehicle from depot to depot. A daily Living Away From Home Allowance (LAHA) is paid while working away, with accommodation provided.  Successful candidates must pass a pre-employment Drug & Alcohol test prior to commencing work. Smoking is not permitted on site and all employees must adhere to the client's strict health, safety, and workplace policies.  What you'll need to succeed  
 
 Current White Card 
 Previous experience as a Leading Hand within civil construction, road maintenance, or asphalt projects 
 Demonstrated ability to lead and manage crews of 12-13 personnel 
 Experience coordinating subcontractors and multiple work fronts 
 Traffic Control experience and understanding of roadwork safety requirements 
 Strong communication and leadership skills 
 Current Driver's Licence 
 Ability to work away from home for up to two weeks at a time 
 Reliable and committed to project deadlines 
 Ability to pass a pre-employment Medical and Drug & Alcohol Screening 
 Contactable work references 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 This is an excellent opportunity to secure a long-term position with a respected civil contractor working on major infrastructure projects throughout Queensland. You'll receive competitive rates, a daily Living Away From Home Allowance (LAHA), accommodation while working away, paid travel time from Mackay, and transport in a company vehicle from depot to depot. For the right candidate, there is also the opportunity to transition from a temporary role into a permanent position while working with a supportive and experienced team. 
  What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please contact Zoe Ingram (07) 4960 1128. 
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

Product Quality

Customer Quality

Supplier Quality

Quality Systems

Training

Health, Safety & Environmental

Skills & Experience

Benefits      Competitive annual salary of AUD $80,000–$85,000 plus Superannuation, commensurate with skills and experience.  Full-time permanent position offering long-term career stability.  Supportive and collaborative work environment with an established retail business.  Opportunities for ongoing training, professional development and career progression.  Exposure to all aspects of retail and convenience store management in a dynamic and customer-focused environment.  Employee support from an experienced management team.  Opportunity to contribute to the continued growth and success of a well-established petrol station and convenience store. Lead, supervise, train and support retail staff to ensure efficient store operations and high customer service standards.  Prepare employee rosters, allocate duties and monitor staff performance.  Manage inventory levels, stock ordering, merchandising and supplier coordination to maintain product availability.  Monitor fuel and retail sales performance and implement strategies to improve sales and profitability.  Ensure accurate cash handling, banking procedures, daily reconciliations and point-of-sale (POS) operations.  Resolve customer enquiries and complaints professionally while maintaining high service standards.  Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements, fuel handling procedures, food safety standards and company policies.  Monitor store presentation, merchandising displays and cleanliness to maximise customer experience.  Prepare operational reports and assist with budgeting, cost control and business performance monitoring.  Keep abreast of market trends to determine the need for improvements in the store.  Analyze sales and revenue reports and make forecasts.  Ensure the store fulfils all legal health and safety guidelines.  Determine product mix, stock levels, and service standards.  Formulate and implement purchasing and marketing policies and set prices.  Promote and advertise the establishment’s goods and services.  Sell goods and services to customers and advise them on product use.  Maintain records of stock levels and financial transactions.  Undertake budgeting for the establishment.    Qualification & experience      Relevant qualification in Retail Management, Business, Management or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant industry experience.  1–2 years of relevant experience in a retail management or supervisory role within a customer-focused retail environment.  Demonstrated ability to plan, organise and coordinate retail operations to achieve business objectives.  Strong leadership, people management and staff supervision skills, with the ability to motivate and develop a high-performing team.  Experience in inventory management, stock control, merchandising and supplier coordination.  Sound knowledge of point-of-sale (POS) systems, cash handling and retail operational procedures.  Excellent communication, interpersonal and customer service skills.  Strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail.  Sound understanding of workplace health and safety, retail compliance requirements and operational best practices.  Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced retail environment while maintaining high standards of customer service and operational efficiency.
